title: A 'normal' resting heart rate was never the finish line.
deck: Higher risk per 10 bpm higher resting heart rate — young adults

statement.detail: No cliff edge in the data — every 10 beats per minute higher tracked with higher risk, decades before old age.

_provenance.paper: doi:10.1136_openhrt-2026-004279 · Chen et al. 2026, Open Heart · population-based prospective cohort, n=12,232, median 17.8y (primary) / 27.6y (validation)

claims.value_on_screen: 26% = HR 1.26 [1.07-1.50] per +10 bpm, all-cause mortality, primary cohort
claims.quote: Each 10 beats per minute higher RHR was associated with higher all-cause mortality (primary cohort: HR, 1.26; 95% CI 1.07 to 1.50; validation: HR, 1.17; 95% CI 1.12 to 1.22).

claims.value_on_screen: 18% = HR 1.18 [1.08-1.29] per +10 bpm, CVD mortality, validation cohort
claims.quote: In validation, RHR predicted non-CVD (HR, 1.17; 95% CI 1.11 to 1.23) and CVD (HR, 1.18; 95% CI 1.08 to 1.29) mortality about equally.

_provenance.reveal_test: Headline names the 'normal range' belief and withholds the replacement (a per-beat slope); the bars supply it.
_provenance.note: Bars are two outcomes from the same paper; c2 is the validation cohort — attributed in the caption.
